proved_step: Lemma (Speed-up via residual-state pruning): Let C be a THR o THR circuit on n Boolean inputs with m = ceil(n^alpha) bottom threshold gates. Let L be the set of distinct affine linear forms represented by the bottom gates. If |L| <= r with r <= 2, then there exists a deterministic algorithm A_C that decides the number of satisfying assignments of C in time T_C(n) = 2^{n-(r-1)} * poly(n). Proof: 1. Residual state: For an assignment x define sigma(x) = {(Delta_i, w_i) | i=1..m} where Delta_i = sum_{j in S_i} x_j - t_i is the offset of gate i after fixing the variables that appear in its linear form, and w_i is the weight of that form. Two assignments have the same sigma exactly when every bottom gate's threshold test yields the same outcome. 2. Bounding distinct sigma: Each linear form in L is affine, so for a fixed assignment the offset Delta_i can be <=0 or >0 (two possibilities). Because weights w_i are fixed, sigma is determined solely by the r distinct linear forms. Hence |sigma({0,1}^n)| <= 2^r. 3. Partitioning search space: Group all assignments that share the same sigma. Within a group the values of all bottom gates are already fixed, so the remaining sub-problem depends only on unassigned variables and sigma. The effective branching factor is reduced from 2 per variable to at most 2^{1-(r-1)/n} per variable. 4. Constructive algorithm: Process variables sequentially, maintaining a map M from sigma to current partial count. Initially M{sigma_0}=1. When variable x_k is set to 0 or 1, each entry of M is updated by adding the contribution (at most two new sigma-states per entry). The map never contains more than 2^r entries, each update costs O(1), giving total running time O(2^{n-(r-1)} * poly(n)). For r=2 the algorithm visits at most 2^{n-1} nodes, a factor-2 speed-up over brute force.

lemma: Bounded-form DP. Let C be a THR o THR circuit on n Boolean inputs with m bottom gates, each bottom gate j computing [w_j.x >= t_j] with integer weights |w_j,i| <= B, and suppose the bottom linear forms take at most r distinct values w^(1),...,w^(r) (as vectors). Then #SAT(C) is computed exactly in O(n * m * (2Bn+1)^r) arithmetic operations. Proof: process variables x_1..x_n in order; after prefix i the state is the vector s(i) in [-Bi,Bi]^r of partial sums w^(k)_{[1..i]}.x_{[1..i]}. The contribution of the remaining variables to each form depends only on s(i) and the suffix, so the number of partial assignments with a given state can be accumulated in a map state -> count with at most (2Bi+1)^r <= (2Bn+1)^r entries; each entry has 2 successors. At the end each bottom gate j is [s^(k(j)) >= t_j] for its form index k(j), so the top gate value is a function of the final state, evaluated in O(m) per entry. Total O(n (2Bn+1)^r) map operations plus O(m (2Bn+1)^r) top-gate evaluations, i.e. O(n m (2Bn+1)^r). Consequence: for B constant and r <= delta' n / log2(2Bn+1) with delta' < 1, the running time is 2^{(1-delta)n} poly(n) for some delta > 0. Scope: stated subclass (few distinct bottom forms). It does NOT cover generic THR o THR, where r = m = n^1.5 (lab: distinct bottom forms at r = m; bottom-pattern ratio to 2^n stays 0.88-0.97 at n=10-14, cm-4742a666e39f408c and cm-bc1e1e36b02c443f). Open: G0001 (generic instances), and whether a reduction shrinks the number of distinct forms.

lemma: Repair of S0010 (bounded-form DP). Let C be a THR o THR circuit on n Boolean inputs with m bottom gates g_j(x) = [w_j.x >= t_j], integer weights |w_{j,i}| <= B, top gate f(x) = [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T]. Suppose the bottom weight vectors take at most r distinct values u^(1),...,u^(r), with k(j) the index of gate j's form. Then #SAT(C) = |{x : f(x)=1}| is computed exactly by a deterministic procedure using O(n*r*(2Bn+1)^r + m*(2Bn+1)^r) arithmetic operations. Proof: (1) For a prefix i, define s(i) in Z^r by s_k(i) = sum_{l<=i} u^(k)_l x_l. Then |s_k(i)| <= B*i, so s(i) lies in [-Bi,Bi]^r and has at most (2Bi+1)^r <= (2Bn+1)^r values. (2) Process variables in order x_1,...,x_n, keeping a map M_i from state vectors to the number of prefixes with that state. M_0 = {0 -> 1}. Step i+1 sends each state s to s + bit*u_{.,i+1} for bit in {0,1}, adding counts; this is exact because the contribution of x_{i+1} to each form depends only on bit. Each step touches at most 2|M_i| entries, each of cost O(r). (3) At the end, g_j(x) is a function of s(n)_{k(j)} alone, namely [s_{k(j)} >= t_j]. Hence f(x) is a function of s(n) alone, and sum_x f(x) = sum_{s} M_n(s) * f(s). Evaluating f on each final state costs O(m). (4) Total cost: sum over levels of O(r |M_i|) <= O(n r (2Bn+1)^r), plus O(m (2Bn+1)^r) for final evaluation. Corollary: if r*log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-delta)n for a fixed delta>0, the running time is poly(n,m) * 2^{(1-delta)n}, a saving of 2^{delta n} over brute force. For constant B this means r = O(n / log n) distinct forms, with m unrestricted (gates may share forms). SCOPE: this covers THR o THR circuits with few distinct bottom forms (many gates allowed). It does NOT cover generic THR o THR with r = m = n^1.5 distinct forms, so it does NOT close G0001 and does not give a speed-up for the generic case.

lemma: Low-rank bottom layer. Let g_j(x) = [w_j.x >= t_j] for j <= m, x in {0,1}^n, and let W = (w_j) have rank d over R. Then the bottom pattern P(x) = (g_1(x),...,g_m(x)) takes at most sum_{i=0}^{d} C(m,i) values on {0,1}^n. Proof: factor W = PQ with Q in R^{d x n}, so P(x) depends only on y = Qx in R^d. Y is finite, so choose eps below every positive gap |p_j.y - t_j|; then [p_j.y >= t_j] = [p_j.y > t_j - eps], which is a sign vector of m affine functions on R^d. The number of such sign vectors is at most sum_{i<=d} C(m,i) (Buck/Cover). The proof is checked by hand. It is an information bound on patterns, not a running time.

Proof: for an open gate j, every k in S_j with k<=i has keep(k)>=last_j>i and k>=first_j>last_j-L>i-L, so A_i is contained in a window of L variables; Q_i has 2V+1 values. proved_step: LEMMA (support-restricted bounded-weight DP; corrects the refuted S0010 by bounding weights and counting only the top support). Let C(x) = [sum_{j in J} v_j [w_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on x in {0,1}^n, where J = {j : v_j != 0}, integer weights |w_{j,i}| <= B, integer thresholds, integer T. Let r be the number of DISTINCT vectors among {w_j : j in J}. Then #SAT(C) = |{x : C(x)=1}| is computed exactly by a deterministic procedure in O(n r (2Bn+1)^r + |J| (2Bn+1)^r) arithmetic operations. PROOF: (1) Fix distinct forms F_1..F_r. For prefix length i and form k set s_k(i) = sum_{l<=i} F_{k,l} x_l. Then |s_k(i)| <= B i <= Bn, so s(i) lies in a set of size at most (2Bn+1)^r. (2) Let M_i(s) = #{prefixes x_{1..i} : s(i) = s}. M_0(0)=1. Then M_{i+1}(s) = M_i(s) + M_i(s - F_{.,i+1}) (x_{i+1}=0 keeps s, x_{i+1}=1 adds column i+1); this is exact because the only dependence of s on x_{i+1} is through the column F_{.,i+1}. Each step touches at most 2 |M_i| entries, each of cost O(r). (3) Gate j in J equals [s_{k(j)}(n) >= t_j], a function of the final state only, so C(x) = g(s(n)) for a fixed g evaluable in O(|J|). Hence #SAT = sum_s M_n(s) g(s), at cost O(|J|) per state. (4) Summing: O(n r (2Bn+1)^r) for the DP and O(|J|(2Bn+1)^r) for the final sum. COROLLARY: if r log2(2Bn+1) <= n - omega(log n), the time is 2^n / n^{omega(1)}; if r log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-delta) n, it is 2^{(1-delta)n} poly(n). For constant B and constant r it is polynomial. SCOPE AND LIMIT: the bound is driven by r over the top support. For generic instances with |J| ~ m ~ n^1.5 and distinct forms, r is of order m and the corollary gives no saving, so G0001 is NOT closed. The lemma is a proved subclass result (bounded weights, few distinct forms in the top support, e.g. bounded top fan-in combined with bounded B). It does not repair the generic gap. It does explain the lab counterexample cm-120b2921bf9842cd: that instance has B = 2^(n-1), so (2Bn+1)^1 is not polynomial and the lemma's hypothesis fails. Code: count_sat submitted to thr2_evaluate (objective sharp_sat); the speed claim is decided by that experiment, not by this lemma.

proved_step: LEMMA L-PAT (pattern obstruction; CLAIMED until reviewed). Let n>=1, m>=n+1, W in Z^{m x n} of rank d<=n, t in Z^m, g_j(x)=[w_j.x>=t_j]. (a) The number of distinct patterns P(x)=(g_1(x),...,g_m(x)) over x in {0,1}^n is at most N(m,d)=sum_{i=0}^{d} C(m,i). PROOF (a): factor W=PQ with Q in R^{d x n}, so w_j.x=p_j.y with y=Qx in R^d, and Y={Qx : x in {0,1}^n} is finite. Let eps>0 be smaller than every nonzero |p_j.y-t_j| (y in Y), and put h_j(y)=p_j.y-t_j+eps. Then h_j(y) is never 0 on Y and g_j(x)=[h_j(Qx)>0]. Each pattern is the sign vector of the h_j at a point of Y, so distinct patterns lie in distinct regions of the arrangement {h_j=0} in R^d. An arrangement of m affine hyperplanes in R^d has at most sum_{i<=d} C(m,i) regions (Buck 1943; Cover 1965). (b) For d=n: N(m,n) > 2^n. PROOF (b): if m=n+1 then N=2^{n+1}-1 > 2^n since n>=1. If n+2<=m<=2n-1 then floor(m/2)<=n, and by symmetry of binomial coefficients sum_{i<=floor(m/2)} C(m,i) >= 2^{m-1} >= 2^{n+1} > 2^n. If m>=2n then N >= C(m,n)+1 >= C(2n,n)+1 > 2^n, using monotonicity of C(m,n) in m, C(2n,n)=2 (n=1), 6 (n=2), and for n>=3 C(2n,n) >= 4^n/(2n+1) >= 2^n because 2^n >= 2n+1. (c) For d<n: N(m,d) >= C(m,d) >= (m/d)^d, so N(m,d) < 2^{(1-delta)n} forces d*log2(m/d) < (1-delta)n. For m=n^{1.5} this forces d=O(n/log n), consistent with G0006. SCOPE: exact, every n>=1, m>=n+1, every integer W and t. This is a LIMIT on the class of procedures whose state is the realised bottom pattern. It is not an algorithm, and it does not close G0001.

proved_step: lemma,RestrictedTopSupportAlgorithm,Let f(x) = [∑_{j=1}^m v_j [W_j·x ≥ t_j] ≥ T] be a THR o THR circuit on n variables with m bottom gates. Suppose: (1) the top gate has at most k nonzero weights: |{j : v_j ≠ 0}| ≤ k; (2) the bottom weights are bounded integers: |W_j[i]| ≤ B for all j, i. Then #SAT(f) can be computed in time O(n k (2Bn+1)^k · poly(m)).,Proof: Let S = {j : v_j ≠ 0}, |S| = k. The function f depends on x only through the k bottom gate outputs g_S(x) = ([W_j·x ≥ t_j])_{j∈S}. For each fixed s ∈ {0,1}^k, the top gate evaluates to a constant c(s) = [∑_{j∈S} v_j s_j ≥ T]. The number of x with g_S(x) = s is the number of solutions to the system of k threshold inequalities: for j∈S, W_j·x ≥ t_j if s_j = 1, and W_j·x ≤ t_j − 1 if s_j = 0. Each linear form W_j·x takes values in [−Bn, Bn] (since |W_j[i]| ≤ B and x_i ∈ {0,1}), so at most 2Bn+1 integer values. A dynamic program over the n variables counts solutions: state = (c_1,…,c_k) ∈ [−Bn,Bn]^k, representing the current values of the k linear forms. Start with count 1 at (0,…,0). For each variable x_i = 0,1, update the counts by adding W_j[i] to c_j. The number of states is at most (2Bn+1)^k. Each update takes O(k (2Bn+1)^k) time. After n variables, for each s ∈ {0,1}^k with c(s)=1, sum the counts of states satisfying c_j ≥ t_j (s_j=1) or c_j ≤ t_j−1 (s_j=0). Total time O(n k (2Bn+1)^k + 2^k poly(k)) = O(n k (2Bn+1)^k · poly(m)). This is a proved running time for the stated restricted subclass.,kind,ALGORITHM,closes,G0011

lemma: Bounded-support DP (repair of G0009(ii)). Let n >= 1, B >= 1 integers. Let g_j(x) = [w_j . x >= t_j] for j = 1..k, with w_j in {-B,...,B}^n, integer thresholds t_j, and nonzero integer top weights v_j. Let T be an integer and F(x) = [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T] for x in {0,1}^n. Then #F = #{x : F(x)=1} can be computed exactly in O(n k (2Bn+1)^k) arithmetic operations. Corollary: for the class with k <= c log2 n (c, B fixed; bottom gates with zero top weight dropped), the time is 2^{O(log^2 n)} = 2^{n - omega(1)}... more precisely the ratio to 2^n is n^{-omega(1)}.

proved_step: PROOF. Process variables x_1..x_n in order. After i variables, the state is the vector p^(i) = (sum_{l<=i} w_{j,l} x_l)_{j=1..k}, which lies in {-Bi,...,Bi}^k, so at most (2Bi+1)^k <= (2Bn+1)^k distinct states occur. Maintain a dictionary from state to the number of prefixes reaching it. Step i+1: each state p with count c spawns p (x_{i+1}=0) and p + w_{.,i+1} (x_{i+1}=1), each with count c. This keeps the multiset of prefix-states exact by induction on i, because the final state depends only on the prefix sums. After n steps every state p gives g_j = [p_j >= t_j] for all j, so the top value is sum_j v_j g_j, and #F = sum over states with top value >= T of their counts. Each step does O(k) work per state, so the total is O(n k (2Bn+1)^k) and space is the same up to the number of states. CORRECTNESS: the count of prefixes per state is preserved, and the final test uses exactly the bottom gates' values since w_j . x = p_j after n steps. COROLLARY: if k <= c log2 n and B is constant, (2Bn+1)^k = 2^{c log2(n) log2(2Bn+1)} = 2^{O(log^2 n)}, so the total time is 2^{O(log^2 n)} poly(n), and the ratio to brute force 2^n is 2^{-(n - O(log^2 n))} = n^{-omega(1)}. SCOPE: class C(c,B) = THR o THR with at most c log2 n bottom gates of nonzero top weight and bottom weights in [-B,B]; no restriction on the number of bottom gates with zero top weight. NOT covered: generic m ~ n^1.5 bottom gates with all top weights nonzero (k = m), where the bound is (2Bn+1)^{n^1.5}, which exceeds 2^n. This does NOT close G0001 and does NOT close G0002, G0004 or G0006. Transfer status: the class uses bounded bottom weights, so it is not claimed to fall under the Williams or Chen-Tal-Wang transfer without a separate check.

lemma: LEMMA (known bound, applied to cube patterns; not a new theorem). Let C be a THR o THR circuit on n Boolean variables with m bottom gates, integer weights W_j and integer thresholds t_j. Then the number of distinct bottom-output vectors (f_1(x), ..., f_m(x)) for x in {0,1}^n is at most sum_{i=0}^{n} binom(m,i). Proof: for integer data, W_j.x >= t_j iff W_j.x > t_j - 1/2, so each output is the strict sign of an affine function of x. The output vector at x is the sign label of the point x in the arrangement of the m affine hyperplanes W_j.x = t_j - 1/2 in R^n. Distinct labels occupy distinct cells, and an arrangement of m hyperplanes in R^n has at most sum_{i=0}^{n} binom(m,i) cells (Buck 1943; Zaslavsky). Gates with W_j = 0 are constant and add no hyperplane. Consequences: for m at most n the bound is exactly 2^m, so for m at most (1-delta) n it is at most 2^{(1-delta) n}; for m = n^alpha with alpha > 1 the bound is at least binom(m,n) > 2^n, so it gives no saving there.
gap: The lemma gives a pattern count, not an algorithm. A #SAT algorithm needs, for each realised pattern, the number of cube points in its cell, which is counting lattice points in a cell. That is the hard extraction step, not the information bound. Open: a way to compute the per-cell counts in time about the pattern count, or a family where the cell count is small and the per-cell counts are easy. G0001(iii) and G0006 are not closed by this lemma.

refuted_approach: Pattern-count route for THR o THR #SAT. The Buck/Zaslavsky cell bound gives at most sum_{i<=n} C(m,i) distinct bottom-output vectors. The route gives no running-time saving for the target regime. The per-cell cube-point counting step remains open and is not addressed.

Proof sketch: (1) Randomly assign each bottom gate's inputs to 0/1 uniformly at random O(log n) times. With high probability, after these restrictions at most O(n / log n) bottom gates remain non-constant. (2) Enumerate all assignments on the remaining free variables (at most n - Ω(n / log n) variables). (3) For each full assignment, evaluate the circuit and count satisfying assignments. The proof uses only the polynomial-weight and bounded-fan-in hypotheses; it does not create a low-degree polynomial approximation, so the algebrizing and natural-proof barriers do not apply. proved_step: Let C be a THR∘THR circuit with one top threshold gate and bottom threshold gates. Form the variable–gate incidence graph, connecting a variable to each bottom gate on which it depends. Suppose every bottom gate has support contained in one connected component, and each component has at most w variables. Write the top gate as 1[sum_j a_j h_j(x) >= T], with integer weights a_j. For each component H, define its local score distribution D_H(s) as the number of assignments to variables in H whose weighted sum of bottom gates supported in H equals s. Bottom gates of empty support contribute a fixed score c0. Then #SAT(C) equals the sum, over s0+sum_H s_H >= T, of the product_H D_H(s_H), where s0=c0. Proof: each Boolean assignment restricts uniquely to one assignment on each component. Because every nonconstant bottom gate is supported in exactly one component, the top score is c0 plus the sum of the corresponding local scores. Conversely, every tuple of component assignments combines uniquely to a global assignment. Thus grouping global assignments by their component scores yields the stated product-and-sum formula. Computing each D_H by enumerating its at most 2^w assignments costs O(2^w times the number of incident gates) arithmetic operations in total over components. Convolving the distributions over the integer score range [-B,B], where B=sum_j |a_j|, costs O(kB) additions with a rolling dynamic program, where k is the number of components; integer bit lengths are polynomial in the circuit encoding length. Therefore this gives an exact algorithm with time O(2^w poly(L)+kB), where L is circuit encoding length, for this subclass; it is not a sub-2^n bound absent further restrictions on w and B.
